data.name: Primal Carnage: Onslaught
data.detailed_description:
PRIMAL CARNAGE: ONSLAUGHT

Created By Ashton Anderson

Prehistoric terror comes to VR in the latest installment from the Primal Carnage universe. Slice, shoot, and blast your way through hordes of predatory reptiles as you make your way back to the top of the food chain! Have you got what it takes? The onslaught is here… survive or be eaten!

Arsenal of Extinction

All of your favorites from the trusty hunting knife through to the reptile wrecking grenade launcher. Channel your ‘inner commando’ by dual wielding your favourite weapons!

Immersive Environments

Stand your ground in a variety of rich, detailed environments, from high-tech cloning labs to lush forests and abandoned supply facilities.

Combative AI

Take on the likes of pouncing Raptors, spitting Dilos, ankle-biting Compys, and more! Each species has its own unique AI, and all of them want you dead.

Intuitive Gameplay

PC:O offers an arcade style experience with plenty of heart stopping action and ‘Oh Snap!’ moments to keep you and your friends entertained for hours. Interact with weapons in the virtual space to aim, reload, remove clips and attack dinosaurs in new and exciting ways.

Amazing Sound Effects

From the lightest leaf crunch to the loudest roar, PC:O features an impressive collection of high quality sound effects to keep you immersed in the action.

HTC Vive and Oculus Rift support

Play Primal Carnage: Onslaught on your favorite VR headset!

data.short_description: An experiment in prehistoric virtual reality combat. Fight hordes of hungry dinosaurs with an arsenal of powerful weapons to make them extinct again!

reviews.review:
Primal Carnage: Onslaught stands as an interesting chapter in the history of virtual reality gaming. Developed by Pub Games and published by Circle 5 Studios, the title attempted to merge the timeless appeal of dinosaurs with the then-emerging possibilities of VR technology. Released as an Early Access project, the game shifts away from the multiplayer focus of previous Primal Carnage entries and instead embraces a single-player survival format where players are left to fend off relentless prehistoric predators. Even today, its concept remains appealing: stepping into a virtual world where dinosaurs tower over you is an experience that immediately captures the imagination.

The game's greatest strength lies in its atmosphere. From dense jungle environments to abandoned research facilities, every location is designed to reinforce the feeling that humanity has lost control of its creations. Virtual reality elevates these settings considerably, turning what could have been an ordinary wave shooter into a far more intense experience. Hearing a Tyrannosaurus roar from a distance or watching a group of raptors circle your position creates a level of tension that traditional displays struggle to replicate. The developers understood that scale matters in VR, and they consistently use it to make encounters feel dangerous and memorable.

Gameplay revolves around surviving increasingly difficult attacks while utilizing an assortment of weapons tailored for immersive controls. Pistols, knives, shotguns, and heavier armaments can be wielded with satisfying responsiveness, and the ability to dual-wield adds an extra layer of excitement. There is a distinctly arcade-inspired approach to combat that keeps the action moving at a brisk pace. Rather than focusing on realism, Onslaught prioritizes spectacle, encouraging players to become larger-than-life heroes battling impossible odds. The sensation of physically aiming and firing at charging dinosaurs remains one of the game's most entertaining aspects, particularly for players new to VR.

Unfortunately, the game's ambitions far exceeded what was ultimately delivered. Its Early Access description promised a growing experience featuring new missions, cooperative gameplay, expanded mechanics, and support for future VR innovations. Those promises painted the picture of a title that would continue evolving over time. Instead, Primal Carnage: Onslaught remains a snapshot of unrealized potential. The limited number of environments and the repetitive nature of its survival structure become apparent after several sessions, and the absence of major updates leaves the experience feeling incomplete. What exists is enjoyable in short bursts, but it is difficult to ignore the unfinished edges that remain visible throughout.

There is still value in revisiting the game, particularly for enthusiasts interested in the evolution of virtual reality titles. It serves as a reminder of an era when developers were experimenting with new hardware and taking risks on concepts that might not have existed otherwise. The combination of dinosaurs and VR is so inherently compelling that even an incomplete project can provide moments of genuine excitement. Standing face-to-face with a prehistoric predator is an experience that few games can replicate with the same level of immediacy.

Primal Carnage: Onslaught ultimately succeeds more as an immersive dinosaur showcase than as a fully realized game. Its engaging combat, effective use of VR, and strong atmosphere make it easy to appreciate, while its unfinished status and limited content prevent it from reaching its full potential. Players willing to approach it as a brief adventure rather than a complete package will likely find enough thrills to justify their time. It remains an intriguing example of early VR experimentation and a reminder that some of gaming's most memorable ideas are not always its most complete.

Rating: 5/10
